purpose: Primary-source basis for the finite bidirectional proof-planning contract. Source access does not constitute reproduction of the source's formal guarantees.

sources.title: A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths
sources.authors: Peter E. Hart, Nils J. Nilsson, Bertram Raphael
sources.access: Original eight-page PDF located and opened; selected page screenshots requested. Text extraction unavailable. Historical reference, not a line-by-line verification of the original optimal-efficiency proof.
sources.supports: Historical A* framework combining accumulated cost and a remaining-cost estimate.
sources.does_not_support: Unqualified optimal efficiency, optimality of a novel mixed-representation proof planner, or global mathematical discovery completeness.

sources.title: Bidirectional Search That Is Guaranteed to Meet in the Middle
sources.authors: Robert C. Holte, Ariel Felner, Guni Sharon, Nathan R. Sturtevant
sources.type: Original AAAI research paper, author-hosted PDF
sources.access: Read abstract, definitions, algorithm 1, stopping-rule discussion and stated properties in sections 1–3; did not independently reprove the extended technical report.
sources.supports: MM's specific priority max(f,2g), its carefully justified stopping condition, and why midpoint claims require a theorem for the actual search setting.
sources.does_not_support: Direct transfer of MM termination or midpoint guarantees to a fact-set forward search paired with sufficient-goal backward regression.

sources.title: Front-to-End Bidirectional Heuristic Search with Near-Optimal Node Expansions
sources.authors: Jingwei Chen, Robert C. Holte, Sandra Zilles, Nathan R. Sturtevant
sources.access: Read abstract and bibliographic record; full expansion-bound proof not independently checked.
sources.supports: NBS makes a precise near-optimal expansion statement within its defined model, motivating care with transferred optimization labels.
sources.does_not_support: An NBS expansion guarantee for the custom Horn planner.

sources.title: Theorem Proving in Lean 4 — Tactics
sources.access: Read apply/exact examples and explanations, including conjunction subgoals and tactic combinators.
sources.supports: Backward application of a theorem turns its unsatisfied premises into goals; the conclusion is matched, not reversed as a logical implication.
sources.does_not_support: A claim that the present informal analytical theorem has been checked in Lean.

sources.title: Lean Frequently Asked Questions
sources.access: Read explanation of proof objects and verification by the trusted kernel.
sources.supports: Distinction between tactic generation and kernel verification of an explicit proof term.
sources.does_not_support: Equating JSON rule replay or a numerical test with a kernel-checked theorem.

sources.title: LeanDojo: AI-Assisted Theorem Proving in Lean
sources.access: Read data-extraction, premise-annotation, dependency and interactive-environment sections. Benchmark numbers are not used in the contract.
sources.supports: Proof-state feedback, premise locations, file dependencies and retrieval as concrete infrastructure for auditable mathematical dependency work.
sources.does_not_support: That all dependencies in the project's physics map already correspond to formalized Lean theorems.

sources.title: An In-Context Learning Agent for Formal Theorem-Proving
sources.authors: Amitayush Thakur, George Tsoukalas, Yeming Wen, Jimmy Xin, Swarat Chaudhuri
sources.access: Read abstract and bibliographic record describing COPRA's stateful tactic search and proof-environment feedback; benchmark claims not reproduced.
sources.supports: Proposals should be executed and checked in the underlying proof environment, with failed applications informing the next proposal.
sources.does_not_support: A promise that the project's scientific conjectures can be solved automatically.

local_sources.role: Exact finite-regulator Maxwell–Dirac baseline definitions P1–P6, energy identity, tangent formulation and explicitly excluded continuum/gravity claims.
local_sources.access: Read the supplied contract; numerical evidence remains in the separate round-4 results and verification ledgers.

project_derivations: S2–S4 define the custom fact-set/goal-regression search; no published optimality theorem is claimed for the mixed bidirectional representation.
Independent forward uniform-cost certification supplies the least-cost guarantee in the fixed finite rule library.
S5–S8 are project derivations for the specified fixed-regulator ODE under an explicit uniform positive-margin hypothesis, subject to the mathematical advisor's independent review.
